questions.text: In an adjacency list representation of an undirected simple graph G = (V,E), each edge (u,v) has two adjacency list entries: [v] in the adjacency list of u, and [u] in the adjacency list of v. These are called twins of each other. A twin pointer is a pointer from an adjacency list entry to its twin. If |E|=m and |V|=n, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the Asymptotic Notation of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?
questions.solution:
Go through all edges once (scanning every adjacency list), using an n [latex]\times[/latex] n table (memory is no problem) to remember where entry [v] in u's list is. When you meet [u] in v's list, look up its twin and link them. Each of the 2m entries is handled once, plus [latex]O(n)[/latex] to scan the lists.

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n+m)[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following two statements:
I. If all states of an NFA are accepting states then the language accepted by the NFA is [latex]\sum ^{*}[/latex] .
II. There exists a regular language A such that for all languages B, A[latex]\cap[/latex]B is regular.
Which one of the following is CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: an NFA may simply have no transition for some symbol, so some strings have no path and are rejected even if every state is accepting [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: take [latex]A=\phi[/latex]: [latex]A\cap B=\phi[/latex] is regular for every B [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Only II is true

Both I and II are false

questions.text:
Consider the following languages:
[latex]L_{1}=\{a^{n}b^{m}c^{n+m}:m,n\geq 1\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{a^{n}b^{n}c^{2n}:n\geq 1\}[/latex]
Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=a^nb^mc^{n+m}[/latex]: push for every a and b, pop one per c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] context-free.
- [latex]L_2=a^nb^nc^{2n}[/latex]: needs to match a with b and with c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not context-free.

Answer: L1 is context-free while L2 is not context-free

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both L1 and L2 are context-free.
L1 is context-free while L2 is not context-free.
L2 is context-free while L1 is not context-free.
Neither L1 nor L2 is context-free.

questions.text:
Consider the following languages.
L1 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] |M takes at least 2016 steps on some input},
L2 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex]| M takes at least 2016 steps on all inputs} and
L3 = {[latex]\lt[/latex]M|M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]},
where for each Turing machine M, [latex]\lt[/latex]M[latex]\gt[/latex] denotes a specific encoding of M. Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
In 2016 steps a TM reads at most the first 2016 input symbols, so only inputs of length up to 2016 matter. Simulating M on all of them for 2016 steps decides both L1 and L2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] recursive.

L3 (M accepts [latex]\varepsilon[/latex]) is a non-trivial property of L(M) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable (Rice).

Answer: L1, L2 are recursive and L3 is not recursive

L2 is recursiveand L1,L3 are notrecursive
L1,L2 are recursiveand L3 is notrecursive

questions.text: Which one of the following grammars is free from left recursion?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1: [latex]A\rightarrow Aa[/latex] is directly left recursive.
- Option 2: S, A, B never start with themselves, directly or indirectly True
- Option 3: [latex]S\rightarrow Aa[/latex] and [latex]A\rightarrow Sc[/latex] give [latex]S\Rightarrow Sca[/latex] (indirect).
- Option 4: [latex]A\rightarrow Bd[/latex] and [latex]B\rightarrow Ae[/latex] give [latex]A\Rightarrow Aed[/latex] (indirect).

Answer: Option 2
